articleTitle: A Novel Symmetrically Controlled Interleaved High Gain Boost Converter for Fuel Cell Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: In this paper, a novel two-switch quadratic boost converter for fuel cell systems is proposed. In the proposed converter, two active switches with symmetrical control are employed. Benefiting from this interleaved structure, the input current ripple will be reduced and the equivalent switching frequency is doubled. At the same time, the required input capacitance will also be reduced. The operation principle, steady-state characteristics and small signal model of the proposed converter have been discussed in detail. Finally, the simulation results validate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A Method for Quickly Assessing the Risk of Power Grid Blackouts
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: In order to obtain a systematic method that can form a low-risk power grid topology, this paper attempts to establish a quantitative relationship between power grid topology and blackout risk using complex network theory. To achieve this, we analyze the network topology characteristics associated with blackout risk and propose multiple structural indicators that can characterize blackout risk. The effectiveness of the proposed indicators is validated in typical topology systems and the IEEE 39-node system, respectively.

articleTitle: Adaptable Hybrid Carrier Frequency Control Method for Variable Speed Voltage Source Inverter
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: Voltage Source Inverters (VSI) play essential role in electric transportation system. Optimizing the VSI enhance the performance, efficiency and stability of the electric motor contributing the overall driving experience and range of the vehicle. In the VSI inverter, speed of the carrier frequency (CF) become important parameters to determine the energy conversion efficiency and quality of the output current. This paper introduces the optimization technique for carrier frequency in variable speed drive system called adaptable hybrid carrier frequency (AHCF) switching technique. High speed CF and low speed CF are switching alternatively in each modulation frequency cycle to form the hybrid CF pattern. The frequencies of these hybrid CF pairs are adaptively changing according to the modulation frequency which determine the speed of the motor. The proposed system design is validated with experiments and the results are compared with different CF methods. The result of AHCF method has significant improvement over conventional methods in term of the efficiency of the inverter while maintaining stability of the output power quality.

articleTitle: A Hierarchical Fault Diagnosis Model for Power Transformers
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: Dissolved gas concentration is one of the most reliable and sensitive characteristic states to analyze for diagnosing insulation faults in oil-immersed power transformers. However, the mapping relationship between dissolved gas concentration data and transformer fault types is fuzzy and uncertain. This paper proposes a hierarchical diagnosis model for power transformers. In this model, the concept of Cloud Model is used to establish the basic probability assignment (BPA) under different transformer fault types, and a similarity function based on Pignistic probability distance is also constructed to correct the BPA value. This approach enables the model to overcome the ambiguity in the correspondence between transformer faults and dissolved gas concentration, thereby improving the fault diagnosis performance. To evaluate the performance of this proposed model, 2008 data samples of dissolved gas concentration are used for training the model. The training results are evaluated by three types of performance indices. Comparing with the evaluation results of the model that the classical Dempster-Shafer combination rule is used, the proposed model outperforms in terms of all indices, with recall (R), precise (P) and F1-socre of 93.9%, 93.4% and 93.6%, respectively.

articleTitle: Research on Electric Vehicle Charging Safety Warning Method for Safety Protection
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: In recent years, frequent incidents of electric vehicle fires have attracted high social attention. This article proposes a charging safety warning method for electric vehicles to address safety protection issues. This method utilizes convolutional neural networks (CNN) and bidirectional long short memory (BiLSTM) to construct a charging safety warning model based on a CNN-BiLSTM hybrid neural network model based on the historical charging data of electric vehicles; Using the sliding window method, determine the predictive alarm threshold of the model; Compared with other models through experiments, it was verified that the proposed model has high prediction accuracy. The results show that during the charging process of electric vehicles, this method can timely detect faults and issue warning signals, achieving safety protection for electric vehicle charging.

articleTitle: Power Management Platform for an EV Charge Station Utilizing Photovoltaic with Battery System
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: The development of electric vehicles (EVs) today has greatly increased the reduction of carbon dioxide emissions in the transport sector. The electric vehicles that have been developed have various battery types. This article focused on battery electric vehicles because they are powered by electric motors, resulting in no emissions. The battery in the study system is a secondary battery or rechargeable battery from the electrical connection at the charging station. In this paper, photovoltaic energy sources and energy storage systems are utilized to reduce fossil fuel use in charging stations. The charging station contains a platform that manages the energy used to charge electric vehicles. The main focus is on utilizing energy from solar cells, energy storage systems, and the grid power line as a backup system for charging the EV when the photovoltaic power or storage system is not enough. The EV used in this study was equipped with a lithium titanate oxide battery (LTO) and a communication system within the EVs to transmit and store significant data. Collecting and displaying data on a platform designed to study energy management suitable for EVs is the purpose. The test results revealed that an electric vehicle with a SOC status below 20% takes roughly 30–45 minutes to charge.

articleTitle: Phase Synchronization for Multi-Module Parallel Battery Energy System of High-Speed Train Based on Dual Second-Order Generalized Integrator
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: In high-speed train, the battery energy system (BES) can provide power supply to the auxiliary equipment and carriage in off-grid conditions. As a commonly used grid-tied interface circuit of medium and low voltage power distribution systems, three-phase voltage source converters are widely used in system operation. In order to solve the instability problem of the converter based synchronous reference frame phase-locked loop (SRF-PLL) under the islanded micro energy system, the dual second-order generalized integrator (DSOGI) is proposed. The BES in high-speed train is established using <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V/F$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$PQ$</tex> control for autonomous operation. The DSOGI can extract the positive sequence component and solve the unbalanced conditions. Besides, it can also have good performance under fault conditions. The simulation in MATLAB/Simulink environment can prove the accuracy of the proposed strategy and theoretical analysis.

articleTitle: An RMS Photovoltaic Inverter Model Based on CNS15382
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: As renewable energy generators are used widely in power systems, their impact on the power system becomes increasingly apparent. These must be done through simulation to improve the power system’ s reliability, planning, dispatching, and accident analysis. Therefore, how to establish models and parameters of these renewable energy generators has become an important research topic. The renewable energy generator models used by most power systems simulation software, such as PSS/E, PSLF, and DSATools, are all second-generation models proposed by WECC. In this paper, we built an RMS model based on the WECC DER_A model and Taiwan CNS15382 standards. Furthermore, we used the field measurement of the actual PV inverter following the Taiwan CNS standards to verify the built RMS model.

articleTitle: Impacts of Grid-Forming Converters on Distance Protection During Unbalanced Faults
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: Grid-forming (GFM) converters are employed to emulate the behavior of synchronous generators (SGs) by regulating voltage and frequency. However, their control loops result in exclusive short-circuit fault characteristics that can affect distance protection. This paper elaborates mathematically on how GFM converters impact the apparent impedance measured by distance relays during unbalanced faults in a two-terminal system. The analysis provides the first explanation for why GFM converters may alter the trajectory of the apparent impedance, potentially causing misoperation of distance protection. Electromagnetic transient (EMT) simulations using the EPRI benchmark system are conducted to validate the analytical findings and provide in-depth investigations. During unbalanced faults with fault resistance, GFM converters exhibit positive sequence performance similar to SGs, but the inner control parameters may adversely affect negative sequence behavior, ultimately reducing protection sensitivity. When current limits are reached, the current limits and FRT solutions determine the magnitude and angle of current references, thereby changing the apparent impedance and affecting protection results. For future studies, coordinating protection settings with the magnitudes and phase angles of GFM converter current contributions is essential to ensure correct distance protection operation.

articleTitle: On Site Detection and Localization of Partial Discharge in Hydropower Plant GIL/GIS Based on Ultra-high Frequency Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: Partial discharge (PD) detection is an important method for diagnosis and assessment of insulation defects in gas- insulated switchgears (GISs) and gas-insulated transmission lines (GILs). The ultra-high frequency (UHF) method is widely used for on-site PD detection of GIL/GIS owing its good sensitivity and anti-interference performance. In this paper, PD detection and localization diagnosis of GIL/GIS equipment in a hydropower plant is conducted. PD signal is detected in the GIL/GIS B-phase at the outgoing line yard using the UHF technique. Then, based on localization analysis, it is finally determined that the PD source is located on the insulator between the disconnector and current transformer. According to the PD diagnosis, the insulator is replaced and the X-CT flaw detection result shows that there are two 1–2 mm gaps inside this insulator. Subsequently, the PD test in the factory shows that significant and stable PDs are provoked by the dismantled insulator. These fully confirm the accuracy of on-site PD detection and localization diagnosis. The research of this paper provides good guidance for on-site equipment maintenance and helps to improve equipment stability.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of the Bess System: Contribution to the Primary Frequency Regulation at C.H Marañon - Huanuco
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: The research aimed to evaluate the Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) system for primary frequency regulation at the Marañón hydroelectric plant. The research approach is quantitative, the method is deductive-descriptive, the type of research that was carried out is applied to a level of descriptive-correlational research and the design was non-experimental with longitudinal cut, frequency data of the system was used compared with the frequency of the speed regulator of the Marañón hydroelectric plant, according to the data obtained another comparison was made with the system frequency and the plant frequency after the installation of the BESS system, finally a simulation of the data obtained is carried out to see the behavior of the batteries during the power contribution time for primary frequency regulation. Concluding that, facing disturbances in the Peruvian power system, the BESS system is a good alternative when it comes to stabilizing the network, with the quick charge and discharge that positively influences the frequency, it was also possible to calculate the percentage of non-compliance that was reduced after the use of the BESS systems together with the economic benefits generated by the use of BESS systems.

articleTitle: A Hybrid T-Type Three-Level Dual Active Bridge Converter for Energy-Saving Elevator Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: With the increasing energy crisis and the continuous improvement of energy utilization efficiency, the energy storage elevator as a new type of energy-saving and environmentally friendly transportation has received widespread attention. In this context, a hybrid T-type three-level dual active bridge (HT3L-DAB) converter for energy-saving elevator systems is proposed. Compared with traditional DAB converters, aT-type three-level circuit structure is introduced, which increases the degree of control freedom and reduces voltage stress on switches. Compared with hybrid neutral point clamped three-level dual active bridge (HN3L-DAB) converters, it does not need clamping diode, reduces the loss of passive components, and improves the conversion efficiency of the system to a certain extent. In this paper, the topology, operating principle, and operating mode of the HT3L-DAB converter are introduced. Finally, the feasibility of the converter and the correctness of the theoretical analysis are proved by a simulation model with a maximum transmission power of 16 kW.

articleTitle: Life Cyle Assessment of Recycling End-of-Life Photovoltaic Modules
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: This paper demonstrates a comparative life cycle assessment of four end-of-life photovoltaic module recycling technologies. The results show that the recycling technology for crystalline silicon modules based on mechanical treatment has the greatest environmental impacts, followed by the recycling technologies for thin film modules. And the recycling technology for crystalline silicon modules based on physicochemical treatment generates environmental benefit. As for the environment impacts of photovoltaic module's full life cycle considering the recycling stage, single-crystalline silicon module has the greatest environmental impact, followed by multi-crystalline silicon module, and cadmium telluride module the least. Crystalline silicon modules reduce their environmental impact through the efficient recovery of recyclable materials and the proper disposal of emissions during the recycling process, while the recycling treatment of thin-film modules increases their environmental impact. However, the overall environmental impact of crystalline silicon modules is still greater than that of thin film modules.

articleTitle: Research on Negative Charge Prediction Method Based on Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: Power load forecasting is very important in balancing energy distribution and ensuring the safe operation of power system, and accurate load forecasting can effectively reduce the occurrence of electricity accidents and improve electricity efficiency. Using the advantages of the neural network combination model, the features of the time series are fully extracted and input into the Gate Recurrent Unit (GRU) network for prediction, so that the prediction accuracy of the model is higher and the generalization ability is stronger. In order to verify the proposed technology, 100 data nodes were selected in this experiment, and ResNet+GRU was proved to be superior to all methods by experiments, The values of MAE, MSE, RMSE and MAPE were obtained using ResNet+GRU.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of DC Microgrid Considering Ramp Rate Limiter
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: Virtual inertia (VI) is considered to be an effective method to reduce the rate of change of voltage (RoCo V). Compared with VI, the ramp rate limiter (RRL) could accurately control RoCo V when a disturbance occurs in a DC microgrid (MG), but its impact on the system stability remains unclear when constant power loads (CPL) are included. In this work, the RRL, as a complement to VI, is used to accurately control RoCo V. By modeling the system with RRL, it is demonstrated that RRL would reshape the primary control loop of the DC MG, and decrease the order of the system model. Small-signal and large-signal stability of the system containing RRL and CPL are analyzed. It is demonstrated that RRL could enhance the stability of the DC MG. Furthermore, it is proved that the rate of RRL would not affect the steady-state performance of the DC MG. The proposed method is compared with VI to demonstrate the feasibility and performance of the proposed method using simulation results.

articleTitle: Photovoltaic Inverter Model in an Electromagnetic Transient Simulator Based on CNS15382
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: Because of global warming, more and more countries use renewable energy to mitigate greenhouse gas (GHG) concentrations in the Earth's atmosphere. The inverter is a crucial device in the conversion of renewable energy. Since the response of renewable energy generators is much quicker than traditional generators, using the RMS model to simulate is not enough to represent the dynamic response. Therefore, we must construct an EMT model for a more accurate dynamic response. The Electric Power Research Institute (EPRI) and National Renewable Energy Laboratory (NREL) have published a generic EMT model of inverter-based resource (IBR). Because the grid codes of different countries differ, our study aims to modify the generic EMT model published by NREL to follow Taiwan's standard (Chinese National Standards, CNS). By tuning the parameters in the EMT model and comparing the measurement results, we verified that the simulation results approach the realistic system.

articleTitle: Electric Vehicle Charging Station Resourcing Hybrid Energy from Fuel Cell and Solar Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: Electric vehicles are projected to be one form of carbon-neutral transportation. Nevertheless, the electrification sector has reached 25% of global greenhouse gas emissions. It is inevitable that the transport sector and the decarbonization of our energy system will be connected. The electrification of transportation, when combined with the grid network's increasingly clean energy mix, is a significant step in reducing air pollution and CO2 emissions. Eventually, electric vehicles will become carbon-neutral without relying on fossil fuel electrification, which is expected to decrease gradually. This paper presents an EV charge station using clean DC electricity, which draws energy from photovoltaic frameworks and a fuel cell system to charge a stationary battery to achieve the DC bus voltage balance. In the focused study, the appropriate fuel cell converter contribution is being designed coincidently with DC bus voltage. Experimental results on the voltage stability of the fuel cell converter that connects to the DC bus voltage and the solar energy system were revealed during the testing of the charged battery.

articleTitle: AC Fault Current Calculation of MMC-HVDC System Via Time-Varying Capacitor Model
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: MMC-HVDC has become an ideal solution for the grid connection of offshore wind farms. However, MMC and wind farm have low inertia. Once a fault occurs in the offshore AC system, the fault current increases rapidly. This seriously threatens the stable operation of the system. Therefore, this paper proposes a novel method to calculate the offshore AC fault current of MMC. Firstly, a time-varying capacitor equivalent model of MMC is proposed. Then, the fault current before and after MMC blocking is calculated by the piecewise linearization method based on Nearest Level modulation (NLM) algorithm. Finally, the accuracy and efficiency of the proposed method are verified by comparing with the simulation results of PSCAD/EMTDC.

articleTitle: Enhancing Down-Shifting Solar Cells by Scattering Particles
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: The improvement of down-shifting solar cells by scattering of the particles introduced into ethylene vinyl acetate (EVA) films is investigated. When the scattered short wavelength light reaches the down-shifting materials, it is absorbed and converted into long wavelength light. This extra absorption strengthens the down-shifting effect, and reduces the reflection of the solar cells in the short wavelength range, leading to an increase in the conversion efficiency. In this work, we packaged the crystalline silicon solar cells with CaAISiN3:Eu<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>+ down-shifting phosphors and Y 203 particles. The experimental results show that the scatter by Y 203 particles can increase the conversion efficiency of down-shifting solar cells from 20.522 % to 20.652%.

articleTitle: Qualitative Identification of Vacuum Degree of Vacuum Circuit Breaker by Terahetz Spectrum Based on PSO-SVM
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: In order to realize the accurate recognition of vacuum degree of vacuum circuit breaker, a qualitative recognition method of terahertz spectrum based on PSO-SVM is proposed. Firstly, the time-domain spectral data of two vacuum degrees were obtained based on terahertz time-domain spectral system. Then, the two vacuum degrees were qualitatively identified by using support vector machine (SVM), genetic algorithm optimization support vector machine (GA-SVM) and particle swarm optimization support vector machine (PSO-SVM). The results show that the vacuum degree recognition model based on terahertz spectral data combined with PSO-SVM has the best effect, and the model accuracy rate is 94.1176%. Therefore, terahertz time-domain spectroscopy provides a new and efficient detection method for rapid qualitative identification of vacuum degree of vacuum circuit breakers, and also provides a practical basis for the application of terahertz technology in the field of non-destructive testing of electrical equipment.

articleTitle: Frequency Modulation Control Method of Electrolytic Aluminum and Polysilicon Load Polymerization Based on Active Adjustable Capacity Collaborative Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: In recent years, new energy power generation has developed rapidly, and the reduction of system inertia caused by the high incidence of new energy is the main direction of future development. Industrial high-energy-consuming loads have large power consumption, high electricity cost and great demand-side response potential. In view of the system frequency fluctuation caused by the high proportion of new energy access, this paper proposes a frequency modulation control method for electrolytic aluminum and polysilicon polymerization based on active adjustable capacity. By analyzing the production process of electrolytic aluminum and polysilicon load, the active-voltage model of electrolytic aluminum and polysilicon load is determined, and the maximum adjustable capacity of load is determined based on the real-time voltage state of load to allocate each load control capacity. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed control method is verified based on SFR model.

articleTitle: Design of Overlapping Coil Magnetic Coupler for DWPT System Output Power Fluctuation Mitigation
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: There is no doubt that dynamic wireless power transfer technology is an effective measure to solve the range anxiety of electric vehicles, which greatly improves the user's traveling convenience. In this paper, based on the arrayed transmitter coils, a design method of an overlapping multi-transmitter-single-receiver (MTSR) magnetic coupler is proposed. First, a dual-transmitter-single-receiver (DTSR) system in LCC-S topology is used to equivalently analyze the MTSR system and derive the system output power expression. Then the magnetic coupler is simulated in Ansys Maxwell and its mutual inductance expression is fitted, the transmitter coil evaluation factor is proposed, and the optimal coil spacing that minimizes the output mutual inductance fluctuation is obtained and further verified in Ansys Maxwell.

articleTitle: Digital Twin Model of Photovoltaic Power Generation Prediction based on VMD and Bi-LSTM
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: In this study, a digital twin-based model is presented for ultra-short-term solar power prediction, which utilizes a Bi- directional Long Short-Term Memory (Bi-LSTM) network. By connecting data and physical space, digital twins could increase the precision of photovoltaic (PV) power generation predictions. Firstly, PV system power data and meteorological data are gathered in physical space. Modal components of the solar power generation data are produced by using variational mode decomposition (VMD). The Bi-LSTM network is then used to make an initial prediction for each modal component. The initial prediction result of PV power generation is obtained by fusing the projected outcomes of each modal component. Subsequently, the historical meteorological database is updated concurrently. Similar days are found in the database according to the meteorological data, and the preliminary predicted power is corrected based on the predicted and actual power of the similar day. Finally, comparison results with multiple methods, including Bi-LSTM, K-nearest neighbors (KNN), and support vector machine (SVM) models, verify the precision of the proposed prediction method based on the digital twin.

Author Keywords: bi-directional long short term memory network

articleTitle: Research on Insulator Pollution Degree Prediction and Interpretability Based on an Inherited Ensemble Learning Model
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: Leakage current serves as a crucial indicator for assessing the pollution level of insulators, and its variation exhibits a complex nonlinear continuous time series characteristic. Given this, the paper innovatively introduces an inherited ensemble learning model, which borrows from the learning process of humans. This model aims to commence with simpler tasks and gradually transfer the learned knowledge from smoothed sequences to models that handle the original complex sequences. Experimental results demonstrate that this approach not only enhances prediction efficiency but also improves prediction performance by 29.7%, compared to the traditional baseline ensemble learning model. Additionally, to enhance the interpretability of the model in practical applications, this paper introduces an interpretability method focused on time series. Compared to the black-box model, interpretability results improve the transparency and practicality of the model.

articleTitle: LQR Controller Design for Bidirectional Buck/Boost Converter in Energy Storage Elevator
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: In order to improve the efficiency of energy conversion and energy saving in traditional elevator systems, energy-fed elevators are widely studied and applied. Aiming at the problems of bus voltage fluctuation and slow switching response of the bidirectional Buck/Boost converter in the energy storage elevator system when the power flow direction changes, in this paper, a state feedback control strategy based on robust linear quadratic regulator (LQR) theory is applied to a bidirectional Buck/Boost converter to improve the dynamic response performance of the circuit and enhance the circuit's ability to resist external perturbation First, the state-averaged space model of the bidirectional Buck/Boost converter is derived and established. Second, in order to improve the dynamic performance of the circuit while reducing the steady-state error at the output, the error in the output voltage is converted into a state variable, which is combined with the converter model to establish the generalization matrix of the converter. Next, the state feedback controller parameters applied to this converter are designed based on the basic principles of the LQR algorithm. Finally, inorder to verify the correctness and superiority, a simulation prototype with 1kW output power and 10 kHz operating frequency is built in MATLAB/Simulink.

articleTitle: A Coordinated Control Method for Wind Farm-Energy Storage Joint Systems Participating in Frequency Regulation
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: With a substantial increase in wind power integration into the power grid, ensuring grid frequency stability faces significant challenges. This paper integrates the inherent frequency regulation mechanisms of wind power with energy storage technology to engage in power system frequency regulation. Through an analysis of the impact of wind power grid integration on power system frequency, the necessity of wind-storage joint participation in frequency regulation is elucidated, and a model for wind-storage joint system participation in power system frequency regulation is established. Furthermore, fuzzy control is employed for adjusting the virtual inertia response coefficient, with the energy storage system output controlled based on the state of charge (SOC) of the energy storage system. In the simulation process, analyses and comparisons are conducted between scenarios where wind power does not participate in frequency modulation (FM), wind power participates in FM under low wind speeds, and wind-storage jointly participates in FM under high wind speeds to validate the advantages of the wind-storage joint FM scheme. Additionally, comparisons are made between rotational speeds under fixed and variable coefficient scenarios, along with comparisons of load state and power supply, to verify the advantages of the wind-storage joint FM control strategy proposed in this paper.

articleTitle: Analysis of Electrical Energy Consumption Efficiency Trends Using Visualization Tools
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: Industrial factories tend to use more power. Resulting studying the application of energy efficiency, leading to energy conservation. Through the analysis of the cumulative sum of energy differences Cumulative Sum Control Chart (CUSUM), it is possible to know the trends in energy use of industrial plants. Energy analysis using Visualization Tools for data analysis A case study of a pineapple processing factory To find the efficiency of energy use. The advantage is that you can identify correlations between operations and results faster, and can provide real-time system information for users to make decisions. Therefore, in the research, Analysis of Electrical Energy Consumption Efficiency Trends using Visualisation Tools, using the Power BI program to display the results on the dashboard page on Power BI, which can display the results of energy consumption in real time and can analyze complex data. Using Power BI displays the Dashboard page. It was found that in Phase 1, during weeks 1–54, there were no energy conservation measures, with a value of Productive Dependent Energy Consumption (PEC), equal to 18.32 kWh Unproductive Energy Consumption (UEC), equal to 308.14 kWh. And in Phase 2, during weeks 54-108, measures were set. Energy conservation has a PEC value of 9.27 kWh and a UEC value of 117.75 kWh, resulting in a PEC reduction of 49.40%. By following these steps and leveraging Power BI's capabilities, you can gain valuable insights into your electrical energy use, forecast future trends, and identify areas for significant efficiency improvements.

articleTitle: Analysis of Propagation Law of Electromagnetic Wave During VFT Process in GIS
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: The propagation law of the electromagnetic wave during the very fast transient (VFT) process remains unclear, and it may be a reason for the breakdown. In this paper, the propagation of the electromagnetic wave in the gas insulated switchgear (GIS) is analyzed. Both the axial breakdown and the radial breakdown are considered. The simulations are performed in the frequency domain and the time domain. The results show that the electromagnetic wave keeps TEM mode during its propagation in GIS, and thus it will hardly lead to the strengthening of the electric field in some direction. The defects and the amplitude of VFTO may be the reason for the breakdown.

articleTitle: Architecture Design and Control Strategy Research of 5G Aggregation Controller for Vehicle Network Interaction
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: The electric vehicle industry is developing rapidly, and charging operators are an important medium for achieving vehicle network interaction, which can meet the scheduling needs of the power grid. This article designs a 5G aggregation controller architecture for vehicle network interaction in charging stations and verifies the feasibility of the regulation strategy. This article first designs a 5G aggregator framework for charging stations, including hardware architecture and software architecture; Secondly, the software and hardware structure of the 5G aggregation controller was analyzed, and its safety protection and reliability were studied. According to the principle of more efficient allocation, a power rolling control strategy for charging stations based on State of Charge(SOC) interval segmentation was proposed; Finally, through verification, it was found that the on-site regulation strategy adopted by the 5G aggregation controller can achieve functions such as high-speed interactive communication between charging stations, resource perception, and power closed-loop control, and can respond to the load regulation needs of the power grid.

articleTitle: Optimization and Dynamic Analysis of a Natural Gas Assisted LCPV/T Triple-generation System
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: This paper presents an optimization analysis method of the natural gas assisted low-concentrating photovoltaic/thermal (LCPV/T) triple-generation system. The main energy sources of this triple-generation system are solar energy and nature gas, to achieve the purpose of year-round supply of cooling, heating and electricity to the building. The system comprises of a low-concentrating photovoltaic/thermal system, heat pump, absorption chiller, water tanks, and capillary network. The core of the whole system is the low-concentrating photovoltaic/thermal system, used for space heating, electrical production, space cooling and domestic hot water preheating. In particular, an operation strategy and integrated optimization model are established in order to reduce the life cycle costs. Furthermore, a penalty function is implemented in order to balance lab room comfort with operating costs of the triple-generation system. The construction of the whole system, the realization of the operation strategy and the optimization calculation are all realized by TRNSYS software.

articleTitle: Study on Gap Distance Optimization of UHVDC Converter Transformer AC Side
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: The majority of the already constructed Ultra High Voltage (UHV) converter stations are situated at relatively low altitudes. The values of air gap are generally chosen according to the maximum specified in the regulations, and this doesn't significantly impact the layout dimensions of the distribution devices. However, in high altitude regions, there are significant differences in the air gap values for various gap shapes. Adhering to the same principle in these areas might lead to issues such as selecting excessively large gap distances, thereby increasing site preparation costs and implementation complexity. This paper, based on full-scale test data from areas at altitudes of 55m and 4300m, conducts a comparative analysis of the gap test characteristics for different voltage-sharing ring at the end of equipment to voltage-sharing ring. By combining this analysis with past engineering experiences, it proposes a rational selection of air gap values. These findings offer technical support for the design of UHV converter stations in high altitude regions.

articleTitle: Optimal Planning for Water and Electricity Cogeneration Microgrid with Green Hydrogen Internal Combustion Engine on Island
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: High carbon emissions and fresh water shortage present significant challenges for independent islands. This paper proposes an effective solution through the implementation of a zero-carbon microgrid (ZCM) featuring desalination plants and Green Hydrogen Internal Combustion Engines (GHICE). An optimal planning method is proposed to meet the demand for environmentally friendly energy and water supply. Firstly, a water and electricity cogeneration ZCM with GHICE is proposed. By utilizing the waste heat of GHICE, fresh water is prepared. Hydrogen production and storage system can absorb excess renewable energy and provide fuel for GHICE. The optimal planning model of the ZCM is then established and solved. Simulation results indicate the effectiveness of the proposed method in improving economy, reducing carbon emissions and promoting the absorption and penetration of wind and photovoltaic power.

articleTitle: Day-ahead to Intraday Power Scheduling Model Considering Temperature Optimization of Alkaline Water Electrolyzers
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: A two-timescale optimal scheduling model for Day-ahead and intraday operation considering the Temperature Optimization (D- I-TO model) of alkaline water electrolyzers is proposed to optimize the economic efficiency of Renewable Power-to-Hydrogen System (RPHS). Three electro-thermal char-acteristics of the alkaline water electrolyzers are considered, of which the maximum power (MMP) function and efficiency function are fitted to transfer the proposed model into a QCQP (Quadratically Constrained Quadratic Programming) problem. Finally, case studies verify that the D- I-TO model outperforms the traditional model with constant operation temperature CT model in terms of economic efficiency. Furthermore, the D- I-TO model successfully tracks the scheduling results of the day-ahead model. This ensures that the RPHS operates according to the planned schedule. Additionally, the D- I-TO model contributes to a low curtailment rate of renewable energy, indicating effective utilization of renewable resources.

articleTitle: Offline Parameter Identification for Medium-Voltage Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machine
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: This paper describes a novel offline parameter identification technique, specifically for medium voltage interior permanent magnet synchronous machine driven by Cascaded H-Bridge inverter. Accurate identification of parameters is indispensable to correct decoupling of current loop in vector control. Unlike low voltage permanent magnet synchronous machines commonly driven by the conventional six-switch inverter, the proposed method specifically focuses on medium voltage applications and takes advantage of the topology of cascaded H bridge to tune machine parameters of resistance, d-axis inductance, q-axis inductance and magnetic flux linkage. By properly modifying the topology structure, the accuracy of identification can be improved with issues like voltage drop across semiconductor devices and low duty ratio considered. In the end, the paper presents simulation results using proposed technique, followed by theoretical analysis as proof of the feasibility of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Intelligent Safety Power Supply System Based on Grounding Form Transformation
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: Driven by the global energy transition and the double carbon goals, the construction of smart grids has raised higher demands for the safety and reliability of power systems. This study proposes an intelligent safety power supply solution based on grounding form transformation, aiming to enhance the state monitoring and fault early warning response capabilities of electrical equipment through the transformation of grounding configurations. The power supply system comprises key components such as isolation transformers, insulation monitoring devices, and alarm display units. It achieves real-time surveillance of the electrical equipment operational status through insulation monitoring and fault diagnosis techniques. Experimental results demonstrate that the system can monitor insulation conditions effectively and issue alarms in abnormal situations promptly. The hardware and software adopt a modular design, and multiple iterations of optimization ensure the stability of the system in a variety of electrical environments. This research provides innovative technical support for the electrical safety and reliability of smart grids, offering a solid theoretical foundation for further research and application in related fields.

articleTitle: Research on Convergence Characteristics of High Voltage Flyback Converter Feeding Capacitive Load
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: The boost time of the flyback converter must meet specific requirements to accommodate the rapid arming response of initiation and ignition system. This paper presents dynamic models of the flyback converter and analyzes its operational principles and energy conversion. The analysis reveals that energy conversion cannot be completed during the boosting process startup stage, resulting in peak primary and secondary currents several times higher than steady-state current. Implementing high-frequency and low-duty cycle control during startup can reduce these peaks. Furthermore, the convergent characteristics of flyback converters feeding capacitive load are studied. It has been observed that boost time is proportional to frequency when duty cycle remains constant. The accuracy of the theoretical model has been validated through simulation and experimental results.

articleTitle: Optimal Integration of Phase Shifter as Power Flow Controllers in Transmission Network Expansion
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: Phase shifting transformers are devices that allow transmission system operators to control active power flow, and their use has increased over the last years. This paper proposes a mathematical optimization model for transmission network expansion considering the incorporation of phase shifting transformers. The performance of the proposed model was analyzed using the 9-bus IEEE test system and considering an annual load demand growth of 5%. Simulation results indicate that lower investment costs are needed if phase shifting transformers are considered in the optimization model compared to the investment costs when only transmission lines are considered in the optimization model. Furthermore, the results indicate that if neither transmission lines nor phase shifting transformers are incorporated into the test system over the planning period, the total load demand cannot be supplied.

articleTitle: Optimal Operation of Railway Traction Power System with PV and Energy Storage Considering Flexible Voltage Unbalance Constraints
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: The flexible traction power system (FTPS) integrates photovoltaic and energy storage via the railway power flow controller, providing an effective solution for addressing problems like low energy utilization and voltage unbalance (VU) in split-phase traction power systems. This paper proposes an optimal dispatch method for the flexible traction power system while considering VU regulation. By utilizing the flexibility given by the chance limits in the VU standard, flexible VU constraints are proposed for split-phase FTPS, which can relieve the VU compensation capability requirements. Then, an optimal operation model of FTPS is proposed, taking minimal daily operational cost as the objective and incorporating flexible VU constraints. The numerical results show that the proposed method can realize the optimal economical operation of split-phase FTPS while ensuring VU performance. Compared to the existing methods with the fixed VU constraint, it can avoid the optimization model's infeasibility in case of load increase.

articleTitle: Fast and Accurate Recovery Optimization Method for Active Load Considering Demand Response
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: In order to solve the problem of load recovery after load cutting caused by the phenomena of low-frequency and low-voltage and insufficient generation capacity, this paper proposes a fast and accurate recovery optimization model of active load considering demand response and gives the dynamic solution process. The model divides the active load recovery into two parts, the first part is the downward regulation process of load-side resources, which provides more space for load recovery and thus improves the efficiency of load recovery, and the second part is the process of accurate load recovery. The model is able to restore load quickly and accurately while ensuring system frequency security and minimizing the adverse effects of power outages on users. The model is solved dynamically in an IEEE-33 node system, and the results show that the proposed model is able to give an accurate load recovery scheme that guarantees frequency dynamic safety and tidal current safety, and the recovery speed is faster.

articleTitle: SET-CNN Based Line Selection Method for Grounding Fault in Distribution Network
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: To solve the problem that the input data can not reflect the difference between fault line and non-fault line, which leads to low accuracy of line selection, a method of fault line selection based on synchroextracting transform (SET) and convolutional neural network (CNN) is proposed. The basic principles of SET and CNN are investigated, and based on them, a new line selection method is studied. CNN autonomously learns fault features in SET time-frequency images to realize image classification, which simultaneously implies that fault line is selected. The comparative experiments are designed to verify the performance of the proposed method. The experimental results show that the proposed method can be used for line selection under different fault conditions and improve the accuracy of line selection, with good generalization performance.

articleTitle: Parameter Estimation of Wideband Oscillation Based on Interpolated Discrete Fourier Transform with Five-Term Maximum Sidelobe Attenuation Window
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: With the increasing penetration of electronic devices in power systems, electrical quantities are increasingly exhibiting wideband characteristics, and thus new stability issues of power grid have arisen. New requirements for monitoring frequency range and accuracy of power system signals are put forward. In this paper, a parameter estimation method is proposed to achieve high-precision measurement of the wideband oscillation. A novel method is proposed, using spectral line interpolation Discrete Fourier Transform (DFT) with five-term maximum sidelobe attenuation (MSA) window for parameter estimation of wideband oscillation. This approach aims to ensure the precision and stability of the algorithm, particularly in low signal-to-noise ratio conditions. Simulation results show that the proposed method is more suitable for wideband oscillation detection. It effectively mitigates spectral leakage and noise interference, demonstrating higher detection accuracy and stability compared to DFT with traditional window.

articleTitle: Coordinated Expansion Planning between Transmission Network and Energy Storage Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: Considering the challenge of accommodating the ever-increasing renewable energy generation in a power system, a coordinated expansion planning method for a transmission network and energy storage devices is proposed in this work. Specifically, a segmented incentive-based demand response model is first proposed. Then, by incorporating the demand response model, a coordinated expansion planning model between the transmission network and energy storage devices is presented with flexible regulation capability of the power system considered. The presented optimization models are formulated as mixed integer linear ones and can be solved efficiently with commercial solvers. A modified version of the well-known Garver's 6-node power system is employed to demonstrate the feasibility and efficiency of the proposed coordinated expansion planning method.

articleTitle: Optimization Scheduling of Distribution Network with Aggregated Flexible Resources
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: With the increasing penetration of distributed renewable energy sources with volatility and uncertainty, the issue of insufficient regulation capability of distribution network (DN) has become increasingly prominent. Air conditioners, electric vehicles, and energy storage systems within the DN possess significant adjustable potential. However, their large numbers and wide distribution present challenges to centralized control. To fully leverage the role of clusters of flexible resources in DN scheduling, operational models for flexible resources such as air conditioners, electric vehicles, and energy storage systems are first established in this paper, and then reformulated into a compact constraint space form. Subsequently, an inner approximation Minkowski Sum approach is employed to aggregate the adjustable capabilities of flexible resources. Then, an optimization scheduling model for DN with aggregated flexible resources is established. Finally, the proposed method is tested on the IEEE 33-bus distribution system. The simulation results indicate that by aggregating flexible resources and involving them in the optimization scheduling of DN, the proposed method can reduce scheduling costs, improve the absorption rate of renewable energy, and enhance the operational flexibility of the DN.

articleTitle: Optimized Control of the Distributed DC Energy System in a Building Considering Bidirectional EV Charging
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: Grid-friendly buildings can actively participate in the coordination and interaction of the power grids, primarily by flattening the building demand profile. The increasing penetration of the renewable power generation and the disorderly electric vehicles charging bring new challenges to building energy control. To achieve a flattened building power demand profile, researchers have paid efforts on developing the peak shaving and valley filling strategies. However, the potential of bidirectional electric vehicles charging strategy to enhance the grid friendliness has not been considered. Therefore, this study proposes an optimized control method for a distributed direct current (DC) energy system in buildings that integrates the battery storage system, the photovoltaic, and the electric vehicles. This method considers the bidirectional EV charging strategy, aiming to flatten the building power load curve. Three strategies were evaluated and compared to show the suboptimal performance of the rule-based strategy in relieving grid pressure caused by the building peak-to-valley difference and load curve flatten. Results also demonstrated that the improved performance of the proposed control in terms of peak demand limiting and curve flatten.

articleTitle: Research on Safety and Reliability Evaluation of MW Semi-Direct Drive Permanent Magnet Synchronous Wind Turbine
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: Penetration proportion of megawatt(MW) semi-direct drive permanent magnet synchronous wind turbine is increasing, and the number of commissioned MW wind turbine is raising. With high investment costs and complex maintenance, once MW wind turbine are out of gear, it will cause huge economic losses. Therefore, quantitative safety assessment of the entire life cycle of MW semi-direct drive permanent magnet synchronous wind turbine is crucial. In response to key components of MW semi-direct drive permanent magnet synchronous wind turbine malfunction with increasing operating time, A AGREE-empirical method was proposed to obtain the fault ratio of MW wind turbine key components. Evaluate the cumulative distribution function of MW wind turbine faults using Weibull distribution method, and solve Weibull distribution parameter estimation using average rank method and least squares method. Obtain the inherent safety and reliability model of the wind turbine and key components. The accuracy of the model was verified using d-test and BootStrap method. Further proposed methods for improving the reliability of key components after maintenance. Finally, the feasibility of the proposed method was verified through a case study.

articleTitle: Grid-Connected Optical Storage Charging Station Capacity Allocation Method Based on Particle Swarm Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: For optical storage charging stations, the optimization of photovoltaic, energy storage, and charging facilities is an important factor affecting the economic efficiency of the charging station. This article first simulates the charging situation of electric vehicles in a charging station within a day, and obtains the daily charging curve of the charging station. Subsequently, based on the characteristics of photovoltaic output in a certain area and combined with the time-of-use electricity price, taking into account the factors of investors and users, a capacity optimization configuration model for optical storage charging stations was proposed with the objective function of minimizing total social cost and constraints such as device utilization and queuing time. Particle swarm optimization algorithm was used to solve the problem, and the photovoltaic and energy storage capacity added to the charging station was configured. Based on queuing theory, various operational indicators of the system were obtained, Finally, verify the rationality of the configuration results from multiple perspectives such as the trend of various costs changing with capacity. The calculation results and case analysis indicate that the method proposed in this article can achieve reasonable configuration of photovoltaic, energy storage, and charging facility capacity, thereby effectively reducing the amount of electricity purchased by charging stations from the grid during peak hours and improving the economic efficiency of charging station operation.

articleTitle: Interlaboratory Comparison of Dissolved Gases Analysis in Transformer Oil
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: Dissolved gas analysis (DGA) is widely used technique for the monitoring and fault diagnosis of the power transformers status. Due to improper operation or degraded equipment performance, DGA data inevitable bring in large deviation, which leads to the misjudgment of the equipment status. To conquer the challenge, a boxplot method combined with Z- score is proposed to judge the accuracy of DGA and achieve interlaboratory comparison. The DGA data among 8 laboratories and 28 gas chromatographs (GC) are collected, the outlier data is firstly identified using boxplot method, then the residual data is compared by Z-score method. Furthermore, data from one gas chromatograph which has passed the capability verification of reliable institute in the field is considered as the reference, the accuracy rate of 92 % is achieved by the proposed method. As the comparisons, the accuracy rate of 83 % is attained by the Z-score robust method, and the accuracy rate of 67% is achieved by combining the Grubbs with Z-score, the method proposed in this paper exhibits superior performance. Therefore, it is recommended to use the boxplot method combined with Z-score to identify and evaluate the transformer DGA data, which provides powerful support for transformer condition assessment and digital equipment management.

articleTitle: A Novel Hybrid EMI Filter Coupled with Paralleled RLC Notch Filter in DC/DC Power Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: It is well known that power converters generate common-mode (CM) and differential-mode (DM) electromagnetic interference (EMI), where high-frequency oscillation voltage or current exist in the system. When a CM or DM inductor is inserted in power converter, resonance occurs due to the parasitic capacitor in the CM loop, which exhibits high-frequency oscillations. In this paper, a novel hybrid EMI filter (HEF) coupled with a paralleled RLC notch filter is designed to suppress EMI and resonance in a synchronous Buck DC/DC converter. The CM/DM model of the synchronous Buck DC/DC converter is built, and then the influence of the main parasitic parameters on resonance is also investigated based on the simplified CM/DM model. A paralleled RLC notch filter is presented and analyzed to suppress resonance by properly setting the component parameters. Moreover, a novel HEF coupled with a paralleled RLC notch filter is proposed and its design processes are also established. Finally, the experimental test results show that the paralleled RLC notch filter can reduce 14 dB at the resonant frequency of 3.9MHz, and the proposed HEF has about 30 dB attenuation at 150kHz-30MHz.

articleTitle: Simulation Analysis of Time of Use Electricity Pricing Strategy for Electric Vehicle Charging Piles Based on Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: Electric vehicles are developing rapidly, and a large amount of electric vehicle charging during the same period will have an impact on the normal operation of the power grid. Therefore, studying the time of use pricing strategy for electric vehicle charging piles is of great significance. This article first elaborates on the working principle of charging piles and constructs the system architecture of electric vehicle charging piles; Secondly, a genetic algorithm for the time of use electricity price of electric vehicle charging piles was proposed; Finally, a time of use electricity price model for electric vehicle charging piles was established. Through simulation analysis, it can be concluded that the model established using genetic algorithm ensures the smooth operation of the power grid load, reduces the charging costs of users, and achieves a win-win situation for both users and charging stations.

articleTitle: Fault Calculation for Modular Multilevel Matrix Converter Considering Control Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: The development of offshore wind power presents new challenges and opportunities for the integration into the power system, with the Frequency Division Transmission System (FFTS) gaining significant attention as an efficient grid connection technology. By reducing the transmission frequency, it is possible to decrease the line reactance and charging power, thus increasing the transmission capacity of the lines. This represents one of the highly promising approaches for integrating offshore wind power. However, challenges exist for the Frequency Division Offshore Transmission System, particularly during fault conditions, necessitating targeted research into fault current limiting schemes and adjustments to protection parameters to ensure the safe and stable operation of the system. Current research predominantly focuses on the operational control of the Modular Multilevel Converter (M3C) itself, with relatively scant investigation into the transient fault characteristics at the sending and receiving ends of M3C. Addressing this issue, a literature proposes a fault transient analysis method considering control characteristics, validated in PSCAD/EMTDC. Such studies hold significant theoretical and engineering value in addressing issues related to equipment parameter design, control strategies, and protection configuration selection.

articleTitle: A Method of Setting Electricity Price Cap in Accordance with Coal Price
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: China's power sector is undergoing the market-oriented reforms, and the exercise of market power by generation companies has become a problem in some regions. Price cap is one effective way to suppress it. In this article a method is proposed to adjust the price cap according to the current coal price, which helps the electricity market adapt to potential price volatility in the coal market. Numerical tests are performed, and the method proves effective in producing a reasonable price cap. The test results also help better understand how much the coal price should influence the electricity price, which can serve as a reference to policy makers.

articleTitle: Joint Expansion Planning of Transmission Network and Energy Storage Considering Wind Power Accommodation Capacity
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: The integration of a high proportion of renewable energy sources into the grid poses higher requirements for the planning and operation of the power system. This paper proposes a joint expansion planning model of transmission network and energy storage that considers economy and flexibility to improve wind power accommodation capacity. First, the scenario analysis method is used to simulate the uncertainty of wind power output. Secondly, a bi-layer model is established with upper-layer planning decision-making and lower-layer multi-scenario operation simulation. In addition, a bi-level solution algorithm that combines the heuristic method and mathematical programming is proposed. Finally, the effectiveness of the model proposed is verified through the improved Garver-6 system. A joint planning scheme of transmission network and energy storage is obtained, and the changing trends of economy and flexibility under different wind power penetration rates are analyzed.

articleTitle: Wind Power Forecasting Based on Sparrow Search Algorithm and Kernel-Based Extreme Learning Machine
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: The accurate forecasting of wind power is necessary for the safe operation of power grid with the large-scale access of wind power. In this paper, a new forecasting method of wind power with high accuracy, based on sparrow search algorithm (SSA) and kernel-based extreme learning machine (KELM), was designed. Firstly, the correlation between wind power and wind speed was analyzed. Then, SSA was used to optimize the regularization coefficient and the kernel function parameter of KELM, and SSA-KELM forecasting model was constructed, using the wind speed as the input of the sample. The forecasting result of SSA-KELM was compared with that of KELM. It is proved that the wind power forecasting based on SSA-KELM is effective and its forecasting accuracy is higher than that of KELM model.

articleTitle: Adaptive Frequency-Voltage Active Support Control Strategy for Wind Farms
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: With the continuous development of new power systems, the large-scale integration of wind power into the grid will lead to a gradual decrease in the inertia and disturbance resistance of the power system, and the stability problem of system frequency and voltage becomes increasingly prominent. This paper proposes a coordinated control strategy for wind farms to actively support frequency and voltage adaptively. When fluctuations occur in system frequency and grid-connected voltage, the degree of frequency and voltage drop is calculated to determine the priority sequence of active and reactive support for wind farms. Meanwhile, considering the constraints of active and reactive support limits of wind turbines, an adaptive allocation strategy for active and reactive power of wind farms is provided. Wind turbines achieve precise active support control of frequency and voltage by accurately tracking changes in active and reactive regulation commands. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed strategy effectively suppresses fluctuations in grid-connected voltage and rapidly supports the recovery of grid frequency, ensuring the safe and stable operation of the new power system.

articleTitle: A Two-Stage Robust Scheduling Strategy for Multi-Energy Microgrid Considering Multiple Uncertainties
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: To achieve the economic operation of a multi-energy micro grid under multiple uncertain environments, this study introduces a novel two-stage robust scheduling approach, encompassing both day-ahead planning and real-time adjustments. First, the multi-energy micro grid day-ahead economic dispatch model is constructed based on the prediction scenarios, and integrated demand response is considered to increase the flexibility of the system. Afterwards, the strategy is adjusted in the real-time phase, considering the uncertainty of energy production and consumption. The Column-and-Constraint Generation algorithm is employed to resolve the above two-stage issues effectively, and the optimal economic operation strategy of the MEMG is obtained. Finally, a case study demonstrates the economy and robustness of the proposed methodology.

articleTitle: Implementation Method for Real-Time Simulation of Synchronous Power Grid Across Parallel Computers Based on HYPERSIM
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: In the process of New-type power system construction, the behavior of interconnected power grids has undergone significant changes compared to traditional ones. In order to study the mutual influence between regional grids precisely with real-time simulation tools, it is necessary to break through the computing capability of a single parallel computer and to study the joint simulation of multiple hardware simulation platforms to make further improvement on the simulation scale. This article proposes a real-time simulation method for synchronous interconnected power grids across parallel computers. The AC transmission line is used as the decoupling interface, and the power systems on both sides of the line are calculated on two supercomputers. The communication mode is optimized, and data and synchronization signals are transmitted through I/O devices. Stable and accurate delay measurement values are compensated into the model, achieving cross platform real-time simulation. The method was validated through a small test system, and the results showed that the simulated waveforms of the dual platform and single platform highly overlapped, indicating the feasibility of the method.

articleTitle: A Quadratic High Gain Converter for Renewable Energy
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: In order to solve the problem of low output voltage in renewable energy system, a non-isolated high gain converter is proposed. A quadratic boost structure is used to achieve a high conversion ratio at a suitable duty cycle, the use of fewer components, reducing the loss of the converter voltage conversion, and the gallium nitride power switches are employed to improve conversion efficiency and reduce volume. The operating principle, steady-state analysis, key parameter design and loss analysis of the converter are analyzed in detail. Finally, a prototype with 200 W rated power, 30 V input voltage and 300 V output voltage is fabricated. The highest and full load efficiency are 95.7 % and 94.4 % respectively, which verifies the feasibility of the converter and correct theoretical analysis.

articleTitle: Equivalent Modeling Methods for Interconnected Power Grids Integrated with Renewable Energy Considering Internal Key Branches
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: The development of interconnected power grids and renewable energy has been progressing rapidly. However, current research on network equivalence lacks focus on ensuring equivalent power flow in key branches of the internal network. This paper proposes a equivalent modeling method for interconnected power grids that incorporate renewable energy sources. It focuses on ensuring consistent power flow in key internal branches. The method uses a weighted electrical distance and weighted output sensitivity to identify these key branches. A dual-objective optimization method is then applied to enhance the equivalent effect of boundary power on the internal key branches. The proposed approach is implemented and tested in the China-Mongolia interconnected power grid, showing its feasibility and effectiveness.

articleTitle: Two-Phase Excitation-Based Position Initialization in Incremental Encoder for Switched Reluctance Motor
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: Incremental Encoders (IEs) are commonly used in electric motor applications to control speed and position due to their compactness and cost-effectiveness compared to alternatives like resolvers. This paper introduces a reliable, straightforward, and cost-efficient method for initializing IEs, particularly when mounted on the back shaft of a Switched Reluctance Motor (SRM). The proposed technique involves a sequence that shortly energizes a two-phase winding of the SRM to achieve an alignment, resets the IE, and calculates a position offset using a single phase as a reference. This approach offers simplicity over other methods by eliminating the need for circuit modifications, removing the requirement for current sensors, having no need for IE physical alignment, and requiring minimal one-time setup. Experimental results confirm the effectiveness and dependability of this method.

articleTitle: Investigation into the Arc-Pulling Phenomenon in 35 kV Bypass Live Maintenance
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: This article provides an in-depth analysis of the 35kV live bypass maintenance technology. From the existing power grid context, there is a substantial demand for non-stop live maintenance of 35kV transmission lines. Firstly, the article analyzes the principles behind the 35kV live bypass maintenance. It conducts theoretical analysis regarding potential arc-pulling phenomena during operations. Secondly, Furthermore, this article constructed a 35kV transmission line and bypass system, conducting a maintenance experiment. It documents the current waveforms and optical images captured during the experimental process. Based on the analysis of the results, under the precondition of employing arc-suppression ropes, the live bypass maintenance has minimal impact on the voltage waveform of the line and did not exhibit any arc-pulling phenomena. This experiment provides valuable insights for the practical implementation of 35kV live bypass maintenance.

articleTitle: Multi-Physical Field Simulation Study on Variable Cooling Cross-Section of Overcharged Cables
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: With the continuous development of new energy vehicle technology and the increasing demand for fast charging, the thermal effect generated during the charging process has become one of the important factors restricting the charging speed of electric vehicles. To address this issue, this study proposes to establish a finite element simulation model for electromagnetic, thermal, and fluid dynamics multi-physics coupling of supercharged liquid cooled cables. The influence of different structural parameters of the liquid cooled channel on the temperature and current carrying capacity of the cable core for charging in the supercharging scenario was compared and analyzed, without changing the cross-sectional area and ambient temperature of the cable core. The simulation results show that the cross-sectional area of the cooling channel has the greatest impact on the temperature and current carrying capacity of the charging cable conductor. When the cross-sectional area of the cable core is 70mm2, the coolant flow rate is 0.1m/s, the cooling medium is ethylene glycol aqueous solution, and the ratio of the cross-sectional area of the cooling channel to the cable core is 1.25, the current carrying capacity of the charging cable reaches 600A, and the temperature is 49.7 °C. The research provides a more comprehensive and in-depth theoretical basis for the design and optimization of overcharged cables, and provides useful references for the further development of electric vehicle charging technology.

articleTitle: Multiphysics Simulation Based on Magnetically Controlled Distribution Transformer
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: This paper proposes a new type of magnetically controlled distribution transformer. The core idea is to organically combine the magnetically controlled reactor with the traditional transformer. By controlling the magnetic saturation degree of the core, the excitation reactance of the magnetically controlled distribution transformer can be controlled, thereby realizing the transformation of the transformer voltage regulation and stability. This paper conducts equivalent modeling of the structure of the magnetically controlled distribution transformer, conducts meshing, and finally conducts multi-physics simulations to analyze the operating status of the magnetically controlled distribution transformer through the temperature contours of the core and windings, which provides a theoretical basis for the operation of magnetically controlled distribution transformers.

articleTitle: A Complete Internal Voltage-Based RMS Model of Grid-Connected VSC for Weak Grid Instability Studies
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: Root mean square (RMS) simulation is resource- efficient compared to electromagnetic transient (EMT) simulation, so it is widely used in transient stability studies of large-scale power systems. However, its applicability in studying weak grid instability under the influence of renewables requires further research while improving the mapping of models in different solvers. This paper aims to bridge this gap. A complete internal voltage-based RMS model of voltage source converter (VSC) is proposed with consideration of the outer and inner loop controls, phase locked loop and the DC-side dynamics to improve the existing RMS models. Then the performance of the proposed model is compared against EMT simulations in a test system subject to weak grid instability. The simulation results show that the proposed RMS model of VSC can regenerate the weak grid instability phenomenon with accurate resonance frequency with more conservative stability boundaries.

articleTitle: A Photovoltaic Output Prediction Method for Grid Based on Irradiance Feature Adaptive Clustering
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
