abstract: Accurate photovoltaic power prediction can effectively reduce the volatility and intermittency of photovoltaic output, which is an effective way to deal with grid impact and the basic support for safe and stable operation. It is difficult to obtain featured data other than irradiance and actual operating photovoltaic data on the grid side. An adaptive clustering forecasting method for photovoltaic power generation output based on irradiance features is proposed in this paper. According to the average irradiance and average fluctuation index of irradiance, K-means clustering method is used to classify the weather into sunny, cloudy and rainy days and form adaptive tags as discrete input features. The characteristics of discrete data output and irradiance data combining with history, using convolution length two-way memory neural network to training data set, respectively. Compared with BPNN, LSTM and CNN models, the proposed 1DCNN-BiLSTM model improves the prediction performance in different weather conditions, excavates the characteristics of photovoltaic irradiance and power generation output, reduces the prediction error with as few data as possible, and provides an effective way for the short-term prediction of distributed photovoltaic output with insufficient data on the grid side.

articleTitle: Response Mechanism of AC Fault and Analytical Calculation Method of Electrical Quantities in MMC-HVDC System Considering Influence of LC Resonance on DC Side
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: Grounding fault occurs in the AC lines of receiving end of MMC-HVDC system. Active power is excessively surplus on the DC side. DC voltage exceeds the protection threshold. It is a serious threat to the operation of system. Therefore, this paper studies response mechanism of AC fault and analytical calculation method of electrical quantities in MMC-HVDC system considering influence of LC resonance. Firstly, the architecture of MMC-HVDC system for delivering renewable energy is introduced. Response mechanism of AC fault of receiving end is analyzed. Secondly, an analytical method for calculating the electrical quantities on the DC side is proposed. Response characteristics of the harmonic components are revealed, considering the resonance effect between the equivalent capacitance of the converter station and the equivalent inductance of the DC system. Then, the analytical calculation method of the electrical quantity at AC side is proposed. The transmission relationship of the harmonic component from the DC side to the AC side of the sending end is analyzed. Finally, a simulation model is built in PSCAD/EMTDC to verify the correctness and effectiveness of the theory.

articleTitle: A Transient Voltage Security Analysis Method Considering the Dynamics of Renewable Energy Stations and Impact Loads
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: A transient voltage security analysis (TVSA) method considering the dynamics of renewable energy stations and impact loads in power system is proposed. Base on the physical mechanism analysis of the third-order electromechanical transient model of induction motors, a data-driven method for identifying time-varying parameters is proposed and an accurate impact dynamic model is established to describe the startup process of impact loads. Considering the dynamic modeling of impact loads, renewable energy stations, synchronous generators and conventional loads, differential algebraic equations (DAEs) for TVSA of power systems are established. An improved implicit trapezoidal integration method is proposed to transform DAEs into nonlinear algebraic equations, and a polynomial interpolation function curve correction method is proposed to solve the nonlinear equations efficiently, which is not required to calculate Jacobian matrices. It has low computational complexity and fast convergence speed. Case study on a modified IEEE 39-bus system demonstrate that the proposed method can efficiently obtain the time-domain simulation results of DAEs for the TVSA of power systems and has high computational accuracy.

articleTitle: Sequential Cooling Load Calculation for Office Buildings in Low-Carbon Parks
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: In the current global context of heightened attention to climate change and environmental issues, energy efficiency and building carbon reduction have become crucial factors driving sustainable urban development. Office buildings play a significant role in low-carbon parks, making calculating their cooling loads particularly critical. However, the cooling load of buildings is often a laborious task involving the collection of building information data and lengthy model calibration procedures. Regarding the issues mentioned above, we analyze in detail the composition of cooling loads of office buildings and utilize a cooling load coefficient method to compute sequential cooling loads of typical office buildings. Through real-world case studies in Beijing, Shanghai, and Guangzhou in China, we provide a reliable reference for office buildings' daily sequential cooling loads. This study provides decision-making support for low-carbon park energy management, contributing to optimizing energy utilization and achieving sustainable and eco-friendly building operations.

articleTitle: Vulnerability Analysis of PV Power Terminals and Countermeasures
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: With growing focus on reducing carbon emissions, there has been a significant increase in the deployment of PV systems. However, the increasing number of PV systems makes power system more vulnerable. PV systems are becoming potential entry points for launching attacks against the power system. To tackle this issue, this paper analyzes the vulnerabilities of PV power terminals and proposes countermeasures. Our proposed method is capable of detecting various attacks rather than specific ones and is non-intrusive for PV power terminals.

articleTitle: Operation Optimization of Wind-Energy and Storage Combined Systems: A Study on Synergizing Multifaceted Application Values of Energy Storage
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: Energy Storage Systems (ESSs) are getting ever-increasingly employed in power systems because of their multifaceted application values, such as mitigating the negative impacts of and enhancing the accommodation capability for intermittent renewable energy generation. In this paper, the challenges posed by the inherent variability of Renewable Energy Sources (RESs) based generation are addressed by presenting an operation optimization model for Wind-energy and Storage Combined Systems (WSCSs). A Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) framework, specifically the Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) algorithm and Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) network, is employed to handle the dynamics and complexities of the electricity market. The proposed GRU-based PPO algorithm optimizes the scheduling of Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESSs) with an objective of maximizing their multifaceted application values, such as peak-valley arbitrage in an electricity market environment, error compensation, and fluctuation mitigation of intermittent renewable energy based power outputs. Finally, sample simulation results demonstrate the feasibility and efficiency of the proposed method in exploring multifaceted application values of ESSs.

articleTitle: Spatial Decomposition Calculation Method for Photovoltaic Power Plants Consumption Based on Effective Static Security Domain
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: The scale of grid-connected photovoltaic (PV) power stations is gradually expanding, presenting new challenges to the resilience and accommodation capabilities of power systems due to the coexistence of fluctuating and uncertain output characteristics, as well as the diverse grid connection methods. Accurately assessing the acceptable range of new energy sources at different nodes holds significant importance in achieving secure and economically efficient grid operations. To address this, this paper proposes a spatial decomposition calculation method for PV power plants consumption based on the effective static security domain theory. Firstly, utilizing the effective static security domain method based on real-time scheduling, a bi-objective programming model is established to maximize the effective accommodation space for PV power plants while minimizing operating costs across the entire system. Secondly, employing a priority target programming approach, the original deeply coupled bi-objective programming model is transformed into two-stage problems that can be independently solved. Additionally, robust optimization methods are applied to address uncertainties within the model's parameters. Subsequently, following the proposed method, the accommodation space for disturbance nodes within the system is decomposed and calculated, analyzing both the safety and economic aspects of the system under uncertain PV power plants output conditions. Finally, through case studies conducted on a 6-node system and an improved IEEE 57-node system, the paper demonstrates that the proposed method effectively handles the output uncertainties of PV power plants. It achieves decomposition calculation of accommodation spaces for various nodes within the system, thereby enhancing the system's accommodation capabilities.

articleTitle: Repairing Faulty Distribution Lines with Human Resouce Dispatch Under Extreme Weather Residual Effect
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: With the continuous progression of industrialization and urbanization, the demand for electricity is steadily rising, necessitating the expansion of power grids. The vulnerability of distribution lines to extreme weather events has become increasingly evident, leading to large-scale power outages worldwide, which has garnered significant attention from power authorities globally. In response to the extensive faults caused by extreme weather conditions in the distribution network, this study proposes a repair strategy that focuses on optimizing the allocation of human resources and coordinating the operation of controllable resources to achieve efficient repairs. This repair strategy leverages the oscillation characteristics of the meteorological system during the residual effects of extreme weather events. By strategically scheduling repair activities within a limited time frame, the proposed method aims to gradually restore faulty lines while minimizing load loss in the distribution network. Case studies demonstrate that the proposed method can minimize the losses caused by distribution network load shedding within a limited time period.

articleTitle: Economic Dispatch of Integrated Energy Systems Considering Renewable Energy and Load Uncertainty
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: In recent years, severe weather events occur frequently, which have a great impact on the integrated energy system. In order to reduce the risk, this paper proposes an economic scheduling model for the integrated energy system considering the uncertainty of renewable energy and load. Firstly, a typical electrothermal integrated energy system is established, and its deterministic operation model is established with the goal of economic optimization. Secondly, considering the factors of bad weather, a regulation strategy based on energy storage-grid joint is proposed to deal with the uncertainty of source and load under bad weather, and a two-stage robust optimal scheduling model is constructed, which is solved by C&CG algorithm. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed model is verified by analyzing the scheduling results under different parameters and the response ability under bad weather through a case simulation.

articleTitle: Digital Twin-Oriented Vacuum Current Breaker Model with High-Frequent and Dynamic Properties
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: The vacuum current breaker (VCB) is wildly used in power system, especially in levels of medium or low voltage. However, the accurate modeling method of VCB considering high-frequency transient characteristics and dynamic arc properties, which plays an important role in the field of overvoltage suppression, is still missing. This work presents a method from digital twin perspective, which first builds the logical control model based on the physical phenomena that happened during the VCB operation, then uses KEMA functions to establish the arc resistance model with particle swarm optimization for parameter identification. Combining the logical control segment with the arc resistance segment, the entire model can describe the high-frequency transient characteristics and dynamic arc properties. And finally discuss two aspects for improvements and applications of the VCB digital twin model.

articleTitle: A New Model Optimization Convex Using Wirtinger Calculus for Economic Dispatch
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: The present work proposes a methodology to the problem of short-term economic dispatch of radial and meshed power systems by means of nonlinear programming (NLP). The problem posed will be solved through the cost function of the classical economic dispatch where generation, hydro, wind in conjunction with the energy storage system will be included, using the linearized model based on the Wirtinger calculation for obtaining the electrical power generated in each of the nodes. The proposed methodology will be used for a short-term period of 24 hours with different hourly demand; for this case will be developed within the IEEE 14-bus model and brief modifications are made to the model in order to include the different generation units. Due to the complexity of the system, the linearized model manages to solve it in less time than the traditional model, without having to make simplifications of the system's own characteristics, obtaining as a result the voltages and angles of each of the bars, expressing a minimum error that is the (penalty) for the linearization of the economic dispatch model.

articleTitle: Two-Stage Robust Optimization Method for Joint System Considering Uncertainty of Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: To conduct the green and low-carbon development, renewable energy needs to play more vigorous role in power generation. Through the cooperative regulation and participation in the spot market, renewable energy, energy storage and electric vehicles (EVs) jointly participate in the regulation so as to improve energy efficiency and increase the penetration of renewable energy. In this paper, a two-stage robust optimization model is established considering the uncertainty of EVs' number. The first and second stages determine the bidding plans of such joint system in the day-ahead and real-time markets respectively, so as to minimize the cost. The associated optimization can provide the robust and economical results. Importantly, the modeling in perspective of uncertainty is applied to EVs participating in spot markets in an aggregated manner. To solve this model, an improved column-and-constraint generation (C&CG) algorithm is proposed, which is solved by combination of genetic algorithm and solver. The test results verify the effectiveness of the model and method proposed in this paper.

articleTitle: Analytical Model of Coils with Magnetic Shields of Finite Size and Permeability and Analysis of Effective Coupling Regions
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: Based on Maxwell's system of equations, this paper derives the magnetic flux density under the condition of magnetic shielding with finite permeability and finite size by using the magnetic vector potential and two-dimensional Fourier transform. On this basis, the mutual inductance calculation equation of two rectangular coils and the analytical equation of the effective coupling region boundary are derived. A super-rounded rectangular sub-side coil design is proposed to enhance the coil coupling based on the effective coupling region boundary. Unlike the traditional approximate calculation method that employs a large number of assumptions, the proposed method is an analytical method for calculating the circuit parameters, which allows the mutual inductance between the coils and the effective coupling region to be solved accurately. Finally, several sets of rectangular helical coils are used for model validation, and the theoretically calculated values of mutual inductance are in good agreement with the finite element simulation results and the experimental results, which verifies the accuracy of the analytical expression for the boundary of the effective coupling region. The proposed analytical model can be used for the initial design and optimization of coils used in WPT systems.

articleTitle: Dynamic Research of Power-Green Certificate Market Collaboration System Based on Dual Carbon Target in New Power System
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: After decades of rapid development, China has become a major global C02 emitter. Building a new type of power system and realizing China's “30-60” dual-carbon strategic goal is a major strategic decision made by China in combination with the domestic and international situation. As an indispensable part of China's electricity market, it is trying its best to transform into a low-carbon energy industry. Based on this, the paper establishes a synergistic system dynamics model of the electricity-green certificate market for simulation and analysis. The research results indicate that companies should reduce their dependence on traditional energy sources and actively develop new energy sources. Additionally, the paper discusses the impact of the green power generation system on electricity prices and provides recommendations to promote the coordinated development of the electricity-green certificate market.

articleTitle: iTHD Improvement for TCM Totem Pole PFC Based on WOA Compensated System Delay
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: This paper presents a system delay compensation method based on the Whale Optimization Algorithm (WOA) for the triangular current mode(TCM) Totem Pole PFC to improve the input current total harmonic distortion (iTHD). The inherent system delay of the TCM Totem Pole PFC rectifier near the zero-crossing point of the input voltage can cause distortion of the input current. The traditional system delay compensation method is to correct the conduction time of the switch tube with an estimated delay value. However, inaccurate compensation for system delay may lead to poor iTHD improvement or failure to achieve Zero Voltage Switching (ZVS). The method presented in this paper can find the actual system delay value of the rectifier for compensation under different load conditions, to achieve the maximize improvement of iTHD, without affecting ZVS. A simulation model of a 1650W, 220V/450V Totem Pole PFC rectifier was built to test this method. The results show that this method results in an average error of only 0.1055% between the actual and ideal iTHD of PFC.

articleTitle: Optimal Power System Load Restoration Strategy Considering Virtual Energy Storage and Discrete Load Restoration Flexibility
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: Aiming at the problem of restoration after a power system supply failure, an optimal power system load restoration strategy considering virtual energy storage and discrete load restoration flexibility is proposed in this paper. Firstly, virtual energy storage models of thermal and natural gas systems are established considering the pipe storage, and the flexibility of virtual energy storage is coupled to the power system, which can improve the discrete power load restoration flexibility. Next, taking the maximum load restoration quantity and the importance index of the restored load as the objective, a full-stage power system load restoration model considering virtual energy storage is established, which includes power supply, grid and load restoration stages. Finally, case studies are carried out on an improved 39-bus power system to verify the effectiveness of the proposed model, and the simulation results demonstrate that the proposed model can accelerate the power system restoration process and load restoration speed, increase the load restoration amount, and effectively reduce the loss caused by power outages to users and society.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Hybrid Electric Propulsion Aircraft Systems Based on Optimal Energy Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: In recent years., as traditional secondary airborne energy sources have progressively unified into electrical energy., leading to the development of more-electric and all-electric aircraft., exploration into hybrid electric propulsion technology for aircraft has deepened significantly. This paper first analyzes the energy flow mechanisms of six common hybrid propulsion aircraft system architectures and establishes multidisciplinary parameterized simulation models for medium-sized regional jets with hybrid electric propulsion architectures. Subsequently., based on these simulation models., a comparative analysis is conducted for different architectures under the same flight mission profiles., focusing on system weight., efficiency., fuel consumption., carbon emissions., and other relevant performance metrics., thus validating the feasibility of the established models. Finally., utilizing the parallel hybrid electric propulsion aircraft architecture and various energy strategies, the paper conducts a typical case analysis of key performance indicators for hybrid electric propulsion aircraft under different power distribution ratios during mission profiles. The research undertaken on system performance indicators, energy configuration, and optimization methods for hybrid electric propulsion aircraft based on medium-sized regional jets provides valuable theoretical guidance and practical support for the future development of electric aircraft technology.

articleTitle: A Bi-Level Optimization Planning Method of Pumped Storage and Electrochemical Energy Storage for New Power System
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: Large-scale renewable energy generation brings more uncertainty to the power system, and energy storage can provide flexibility regulation and stability support capability to the system operation. Pumped storage (PS) is an energy storage technology with relatively mature, high-capacity, low kWh cost and slow equipment depreciation, and its consideration in planning can effectively improve the economics of the planning scheme. Therefore, a bi-level optimization planning method of PS and electrochemical energy storage (EES) for new power system is proposed. First, the operation characteristics of PS and EES are modeled. Then, a bi-level optimization planning model of PS and EES for new power system is developed, in which the upper level optimizes the sitting and sizing of energy storage with the objective of minimizing the annualized total cost, and the lower level optimizes the system operation with the objective of minimizing the operation cost according to the planning scheme, and feeds back the operation cost to the upper level. Finally, a solution method of bi-level optimization planning model based on the Karush-Kuhn-Tucher (KKT) condition is proposed, to transform the nonlinear bi-level model into a mixed-integer linear planning model for efficient solution. Case studies on the IEEE 24-bus system show that the proposed method can select suitable locations of PS and EES in new power system and rationally configure the power and capacity of PS and EES.

articleTitle: An Online Method for Monitoring Measurement Errors in Current Transformers Based on Outlier Detection and Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: Monitoring the measurement error(ME) in current transformers(CTs) online is crucial for ensuring the accuracy of measurements, but existing methods that form a large population containing hundreds of CTs spread in a wide area are difficult to achieve in practice for the excessive demands on acquisition devices. Thus, this paper proposes a method that forms a small-scale population with the CTs within one substation. First, it utilizes the outlier detection method to classify CTs into normal and possibly abnormal individuals and defines the range of each error to minimize the disturbance from abnormal errors on the estimation. Then, based on Kirchhoff's Current Law (KCL), the monitoring task is reformulated to a single-objective optimization problem(SOP). By employing the above-mentioned ranges as search boundaries and the Improved Multi-operator Differential Evolution Algorithm (IMODE) algorithm, this SOP can be solved. Experimental results showcase that the bias of the proposed method is less than 0.11% and 5.1′ at 95% inclusion probability, which indicates the proposed method is capable of monitoring MEs in the widely used 0.2S CTs.

articleTitle: Hybrid BiLSTM-PSO Approach for Multi-Metering Point Day-Ahead Electrical Load Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: Accurate individual load profile forecasting is essential for utilities to optimize resource allocation. A novel BiLSTM-PSO approach is proposed to address this challenge. By capturing short-term dependencies in load patterns, it significantly improves accuracy for each metering point. Historical data (BATELEC I, 2018–2023) is analyzed using statistical methods like Pearson correlation, cointegration, and Granger causality to identify these dependencies. A Bi-directional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) network is then optimized by Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) for more accurate daily load profile forecasting. The BiLSTM-PSO approach achieves significant reductions in error metrics compared to the baseline model: 49.72% (R-squared), 17.95% (MAE), 17.42% (RMSE), and 30.88% (MSE). Outperforming alternatives, the Bi-LSTM approach offers superior forecasting accuracy. The results recommend integrating a BiLSTM-PSO model into information systems for real-time load forecasting, improving procurement planning and grid management efficiency for electric utilities.

articleTitle: A Multi-Objective Interval Optimal Dispatch Method for Regional Power Grids considering River Channel Hydrodynamic and Uncertain Renewables
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: The regional power grid (RPG) contains many run-off-river hydropower plants, which are coupled by river channels. A hydrodynamic model based on the Saint- Venant equations (SVEs) is introduced and used to describe the relationship between the flow rate and the water level of river channels. The Preiss mann differential method is used to obtain the numerical solution of SVEs, and the McCormick envelope relaxation and convex envelope relaxation are used to convexify the differential SVEs. Interval numbers are used to describe the uncertainties of the maximum available outputs of wind farms and PV stations and upstream water flow at the boundary of the river channel, and a multi-objective interval optimal dispatch model is established. Finally, the interval possibility degree method and the method which directly searches the compromise optimal solution of the multi-objective problem are applied to transform the original model into a single-objective mixed-integer quadratic constrained optimal dispatch model for a direct solution. Test results on an RPG demonstrate the correctness and efficiency of the proposed model and algorithm.

articleTitle: Exploring the Operating Region of a Grid-Forming Current-Source Inverter
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: Grid-forming power inverters have become essential components in prospective electrical systems. Their increasing importance arises from the growing recognition that these devices can significantly enhance the integration of renewable energies into power grids. Simultaneously, they ensure the preservation of the grid's inertia and strength. In contrast to conventional grid-following inverters, grid-forming inverters exhibit characteristics reminiscent of synchronous generators. They can operate as voltage sources, contributing various ancillary services, especially when energy storage systems are integrated on the converters' direct current side. Regarding topology, the Voltage Source Inverter (VSI) is frequently the preferred choice for implementing grid-forming inverters. However, the Current Source Inverter (CSI) topology emerges as a notably underexplored alternative for these applications. The CSI can operate as a voltage source and employ drop control similar to the VSI topology, with the added benefit of not requiring limitations or protection for the inverter's output current, as the CSI topology manages this. A central concern is the CSI's power handling capability and operational region. This document comprehensively explores the advantages, challenges, and potential of current source converters working as grid-forming inverters. While not addressing VSIs in this paper, the analysis could extend to them, thus offering a comprehensive guide. This study examines the potential of current source converters as grid-forming inverters, explicitly focusing on their operating region. This research enhances our understanding of their role in advancing grid-connected systems and facilitating renewable energy integration.

articleTitle: A Novel Snapshot Selection Method for Proper Orthogonal Decomposition (POD) of Unsteady Heat Conduction Computation Using the Fourier Number
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: In the field of numerical computation of unsteady heat conduction, the reduced-order model (ROM) constructed by using POD can overcome the problem of large consumption of computing resources and storage space caused by Finite Element Method (FEM) models. However, it was found that different snapshot data selected for POD training would obtain different basis vectors in ROMs. And it in turn has different effects on the prediction of temperature fields. Currently, the adaptive snapshot selection can find the optimal snapshot for ROMs' construction, but it also leads to an extra waste of computing resources and storage space. In order to improve the efficiency of ROMs' construction, this paper proposes a method to guide the snapshot selection using the Fourier number. The cases presented in this paper use a Fourier number greater than 0.12 as a criterion for snapshot selection. The method has clear physical meaning in an unsteady heat conduction process, and can preemptively exclude unnecessary snapshots to alleviate the aimlessness present in the adaptive snapshot selection process. It provides a theoretical basis for the snapshot selection of ROMs' construction.

articleTitle: Coordinated Generator and Transmission Planning Considering Flexibility of Grid
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: Network flexibility is essential for ensuring the availability of system flexibility resources. However, existing research primarily focuses on balancing the supply and demand of flexible power sources, while overlooking the flexible transfer effect of transmission network flexibility, thereby hindering planning methods from meeting the current flexibility requirements of the power system. To address this gap, this paper proposes a collaborative planning method for power system grid sources that incorporates grid flexibility constraints. Initially, the paper analyzes how the grid structure influences the balance of flexibility supply and demand and establishes a process for flexible supply and demand transmission at the grid line level. Subsequently, flexibility constraints are formulated from three perspectives: node flexibility, grid structure flexibility, and total capacity. Finally, a two-stage grid source expansion planning method, which considers grid flexibility, is proposed for transmission networks. The effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated through verification using the Gaver-18 node system.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Filter, Wrapper, and Embedded Feature Selection Methods to Predict Load Progression in Combined Cycle Power Plant (CCPP) Startup Across Diverse Startup Classes
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: In the realm of big data, the utilization of advanced analytics techniques, particularly artificial intelligence (AI), holds paramount importance in extracting valuable insights from data generated by combined cycle power plants (CCPPs). This study meticulously compares three sophisticated feature selection methods: Pearson Correlation Coefficient (PCC) filtering, Random Forest-based Recursive Feature Elimination (RF-RFE) wrapper-based selection, and LASSO regularization for embedded selection, aimed at predicting load progression (Generator Watts) during startup using LSTM models. Leveraging a comprehensive dataset consisting of 240 startup processes, each comprising 14,000 observations and categorized into four startup classes (HOT, WARM 1, WARM 2, COLD), this research carefully selects features for each class independently through the aforementioned techniques. Subsequently, distinct LSTM models are constructed for each startup class based on the selected features, and their predictive capabilities are rigorously evaluated using performance metrics such as Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), Mean Absolute Error (MAE), and Mean Squared Error (MSE). The comparison highlights variations in the performance of feature selection techniques across different startup classes. Specifically, RF-RFE demonstrates superior efficacy in the Hot and Warm 1 classes, while LASSO regularization outperforms other methods in the Warm 2 and Cold classes. This study offers valuable insights into the importance of experimentation and empirical validation in selecting the optimal feature selection technique for predictive modeling tasks. While some research suggests that certain methods may outperform others, this study emphasizes the importance of tailoring feature selection approaches to dataset characteristics, guiding practitioners and researchers toward more accurate predictive models and improved real-world outcomes.

articleTitle: Carbon Emission Monitoring Research Based on Electric-Carbon Model
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: Based on electricity data and electricity carbon model, the carbon emission monitoring, using macroeconomic data and energy consumption data, establishes the “electriccarbon” conversion model, monitoring regional carbon emissions and industry carbon emissions. Using regional electricity data error correction model, exploring regional carbon emissions and the relationship between the electricity consumption, using the key industries of electricity data of constructing bivariate ARDL model (autoregressive distributed lag model), to explore the key industries of carbon emissions and the relationship between the electricity consumption, in order to reasonably predict carbon evolution trend, provide a reference for carbon emission reduction work.

articleTitle: Research on Control Methods for Multi-Port Converters in Electric Aircraft
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: With the development of green aviation concepts, the transition of aircraft propulsion systems from traditional fuel engines to electric propulsion systems has become a future trend. The aircraft's power distribution system will evolve into DC microgrid system combining new energy generation and energy storage systems. Due to the high power density and high integration of multi-port converters, they can interact with new energy generation and storage devices such as fuel cells, lithium battery packs, and supercapacitors. Therefore, this study selects a quadruple active bridge converter for decoupling control based on electric aircraft. A model predictive control strategy based on phase shift control is proposed to improve the dynamic performance of the converter. Finally, the proposed power control decoupling method is validated by combining the scaled-down validation platform of the converter with the power change requirements of electric aircraft.

articleTitle: A Cluster Partition Based Optimal Planning Method of Distributed Energy Storage Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: With the ever-increasing penetration of renewable energy generation in power systems, distributed energy storage systems (DESSs) play a more important role in power system planning and operation. DESSs are capable of smoothing load fluctuations and enhancing the accommodation capability for renewable energy generation, and appropriate planning of DESSs is vital for fully exploring their potentials. Given this background, by employing the cluster partition method, a bilevel configuration optimization model of DESSs is first presented to determine the optimal locations of DESSs and solved by the well-established genetic algorithm (GA). In the developed model, both economic and technical factors in power system planning are considered. Then, a time-sequence-based fuzzy evaluation model is established to select the optimal DESSs integration scheme by quantitatively evaluating the reliability, economics and power quality of DESSs integrated distribution systems. Finally, a modified version of the IEEE 33-node distribution system is employed to demonstrate the proposed optimal planning method of DESSs.

articleTitle: Power Grid Project Portfolio Decision-Making Based on Harmony Search Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: With the power grid enterprises will pay more attention to the return on investment and the benefits of investment. Investing from the perspective of efficiency, giving full play to the advantages of various resources, and maximizing the balance of multiple demands within a reasonable range to obtain the maximum return on investment are the goals pursued by enterprises. This paper establishes a model for measuring the investment benefits of power grid projects, evaluates the benefits of power grid projects from three dimensions, and supports the investment decision of power grid projects. According to the evaluation results, the projects with better benefits are screened out as alternative projects, and the investment portfolios of multiple alternative projects are optimized, with the goal of achieving the maximum comprehensive benefits, integrating the investment demand, investment capacity, project constraints and resource constraints, and constructing the optimization model of grid investment, and finally determining the investment portfolio scheme with the maximum comprehensive benefits.

articleTitle: Renewable Energy Accommodation Capacity Evaluation Considering Section of Power Flow Constraints
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: In response to the problem of errors in the current evaluation model for new energy consumption capacity, this paper proposes a new energy consumption capacity evaluation method that considers section of power flow constraints. On the basis of considering traditional supply-demand balance constraints, this method incorporates section of power flow constraints into the constraints, and establishes a time-series production simulation model considering section of power flow constraints. Due to the presence of non-linear elements such as voltage amplitude quadratic term and voltage phase angle trigonometric function in the node power equation of power flow constraints, the model becomes a mixed integer nonlinear programming model. This not only greatly increases the difficulty of solving the model, but also makes the optimization problem of evaluating the new energy consumption capacity of the regional power grid non convex, resulting in slow solving of the consumption model and inability to guarantee convergence and global optimization. Therefore, this article linearly decouples the nonlinear terms such as voltage amplitude and voltage phase angle obtained from the Taylor expansion of the system node power equation, and obtains the linearized node power balance constraint, thereby obtaining a new energy consumption capacity evaluation model that can be directly solved using mature solvers. In addition, due to the mismatch between the total transfer capability (TTC) of the transmission cross-section and the actual system, the evaluation results of the model may have errors. Therefore, this paper calculates the maximum transmission capacity of the transmission cross-section using the TTC calculation method based on the N-1 principle. The proposed method was tested using an improved IEEE30 system, and the test results verified the effectiveness and feasibility of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Modeling of Industrial Park Cyber-Physical Systems for Abnormal Event Load Control and Edge Node Self Organizing Function Migration Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: With the rise of Industry 4.0 and the rapid development of intelligent manufacturing, industrial parks, as the core places of modern production activities, have increasingly relied on Cyber-Physical Systems (CPS). This article proposes a comprehensive Cyber-Physical system modeling and edge node self-organization function migration technology for the demand of load regulation in industrial parks under abnormal events. Firstly, based on Finite State Machine (FSM), a modeling of the Cyber-Physical components in industrial parks was conducted, and a multi-dimensional load and regulation resource model that can accurately perceive, locally control, and dispatch the park was constructed to achieve intuitive representation of the dynamic interaction process of Cyber-Physical in industrial parks. Secondly, corresponding abnormal event models were constructed for natural disasters and general faults, and a self-organizing perception control function transfer method was used to ensure the continuity of perception and control functions in abnormal situations, maximize the coverage range of edge nodes, and thus improve the robustness and reliability of the system. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method was verified through case analysis, demonstrating the ability of industrial park load regulation under abnormal events, providing theoretical basis and technical support for the intelligent management and optimization of industrial parks.

articleTitle: Intelligent Energy Management Method of EV Charging Station with Photovoltaic and Energy Storage System Considering EV Charging Scheduling
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: To capture the charging station dynamics caused by uncertain user behavior and photovoltaic power generation(PV), we propose a deep reinforcement learning(DRL) approach for optimizing the energy flow paths of electric vehicle charging station(CS). By aggregating the charging state of individual electric vehicles(EVs) into characteristic parameters of CS, we aim to reduce the computational burden of time-varying dimensions of state space caused by the uncertain users charging behaviors. The proposed approach facilitates charging scheduling by allocating charging power to single EVs. Through numerical simulations using real-world data, we demonstrate that the proposed DRL approach achieves on average 13% higher profit for CS compared to the rule-based approach, while also reducing the impact of power fluctuation on grid.

articleTitle: Distributed Neural Dynamic Control of Integrated Energy Systems Considering Communication Noise
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to utilize enhanced distributed neural dynamics to address the optimization scheduling problem of integrated energy systems (IES). The combination of neural dynamics algorithms and distributed algorithms can solve large-scale optimization problems more quickly. Incorporating a fractional order PI control mechanism into distributed neural dynamics enhances the selection range and robustness of the entire control system. When an IES unit transmits information to nearby units, there may be communication noise that could affect the IES. To mitigate the effects of communication noise on IES, an enhanced distributed neural dynamics algorithm incorporates a uniform gain function to suppress noise in network communication. Simulation examples show that communication noise can significantly impact the overall optimization scheduling of the IES. The proposed algorithm successfully mitigates communication noise.

articleTitle: Detecting Method of the Key Influencing Factors of CPS Based on Data Mining Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: With the more and more renewable energy integrated into power grid, the issue of insufficient frequency regulation capability in power systems has gradually become prominent, leading to the control performance standards (CPS) of regional power grid usually not be able to meet the criteria. In order to thoroughly explore the key factors influencing CPS and thus possibly take some effective measures to enhance the frequency control performance, this paper proposes a new method for fast detecting the main influencing factors of the CPS of provincial power grid based on data mining technique. This method calculates the correlation coefficients between the series of the values of CPS and the series of the values of regulation performances and the power deficit of automatic generation control(AGC) z units. And thus, the main influencing factors of CPS are identified by the values of correlation coefficients of AGC units, and the corresponding importance indicators of each AGC units (IIAU) are constructed by comprehensively considering the correlation coefficients, mean, and variance of influencing factors' sequences. According to IIAU, the importance ranking of all AGC units is obtained subsequently. It is suggested to preferentially enlarge the AGC regulation capacity of the generators at the top part of the importance ranking, will more significantly improve CPS. Case studies validate the effectiveness and correctness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Two-Stage Optimization for Decentralized P2P Transaction and Ancillary Service in Distribution Grid
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: With the high penetration of renewable energy sources, traditional voltage regulation ancillary services provided by conventional generation may face challenges of scarcity. Microgrids (MGs), leveraging flexible resources such as energy storage and generation units, inherently possess voltage support capabilities. Therefore, we propose a two-stage optimization approach to explore the potential of MGs in providing voltage regulation ancillary services. In stage 1, decentralized peer-to-peer (P2P) transactions are conducted, and profit allocation is performed using the supply-demand ratio (SDR) method. In stage 2, optimization of ancillary service trading strategies is carried out, and a secondary distribution of ancillary service subsidies is conducted using a network loss sharing method based on the Shapley value. This aims to reduce the operational costs of the distribution system operator (DSO). In addition, an improved alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) algorithm is proposed for the distributed solution of the two stages. Through simulation using a modified IEEE 33-node distribution system, the proposed method is validated to incentivize MGs to provide voltage regulation ancillary services at lower costs for the DSO, thereby preventing voltage violations.

articleTitle: Real-Time Calculation of Distributed Photovoltaic Safe Consumption Capacity in Low-Voltage Distribution Network
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: With the increasing penetration of distributed photovoltaic (PV) in low-voltage distribution network (LVDN), the operational risks of LVDN are also increasing. To address the issue of insufficient security and stability in LVDN caused by the inability to fully consume PV output, a calculation method of distributed PV consumption capacity in LVDN is proposed. First, a linear model is constructed to calculate voltage in LVDN, and the model parameters are estimated based on historical operating data. Then, typical scenarios are obtained by clustering analysis. Finally, a stochastic programming model is developed to calculate the maximum PV consumption capacity while satisfying the voltage safety condition. Simulation results show that the proposed method is able to accurately calculate the safe dissipation capacity with less than 1.14% error even when the LVDN parameters are incomplete.

articleTitle: Air Conditioner Energy Consumption and Structural Thermal Insulation of Schools in High Mountain Areas of Taiwan
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: Although the elementary and junior high school buildings in the mountainous areas of Taiwan only account for 1.28% of the total elementary and junior high school buildings in Taiwan, the cold and tough learning environment in winter at these schools should receive more attention. Due to deficiencies in the relevant management systems of the heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) systems, the use of the heating systems in different areas is not the same, and such differences are likely to affect the progress and effectiveness of children's learning. This study simulated the dynamic energy consumption of elementary and junior high school buildings in high mountain areas and compared the differences in the energy consumption of HVAC systems under different conditions, so as to serve as a reference for relevant units to improve the teaching environment quality. The energy consumption simulation results for school buildings at an altitude of 2,200 m with high demands for heating showed that under the condition of an external wall with thermal conductivity of 3.5 [W/(m2.K)] and an external window with thermal conductivity of 6.0 [W/(m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.K)], the energy use intensity (EUI) of the air conditioner will increase by 0.55 [kWh/(m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>·yr)] for every 1 °C increase in the temperature of the HVAC systems. For every 0.5 [W/(m2.K)] reduction in the average thermal conductivity of external windows, the EUI of the heating function can be reduced by approximately 0.12 [kWh/(m2.yr)] per year. For every one level increase of cooling seasonal performance factor (CSPF) in energy efficiency, the EUI of the heating function can be reduced by 0.67 [kWh/(m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>·yr)] on average. Classrooms on higher floors can receive more sunlight, so the heating loads on these floors are the lowest, while classrooms on the second floor have the highest heating load because they receive the least thermal radiation, and they may have a higher demand for using the heating function.

Author Keywords: dynamic energy consumption simulation of buildings

articleTitle: Medium and Long-Term Wind Energy Trading Mechanisms Based on Flexible Contracts for Sellers
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: When participating in the electricity market, the volatility and uncertainty of new energy output will encounter the dual risks of power and electricity price, which leads to the loss of utility for new energy power producers to participate in the electricity market, slows down the overall growth of the new energy industry, and may affect the national or regional energy strategic planning. Based on this problem, this paper proposes a medium- and long-term trading mechanism based on the seller's flexible contract, a method that can reduce market risk and improve trading efficiency. Considering the volatility and uncertainty of new energy and the actual situation of the demand side of the power system, the seller's flexible power contract has become an effective means of medium- and long-term trading of new energy. Finally, the effectiveness and practicality of the method are verified by examples.

articleTitle: State Estimation in Electrical Distribution Networks Using the Wirtinger Method
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: The state estimation is crucial for operating of electric system in real time, the optimization model, kalman filter and neural network areas use in today. Nevertheless, the model that use mathematical exact as optimization have the nonlinear equation for the power flow that are not affine function and it cannot find the global optimums. On the other hand, the state estimation are widely used in power system due to it has the measurement in all node of substation the system is observable. However, the distribution system network have not measurement in all nodes only in substation and the topology are unbalanced. Due to the aforementioned, in these paper propose the optimization model as, traditional weighted least of squares (WLS) state estimation, Weighted Least Absolute Value (LAV), Quadratic Constant Criterion (QC) and a new model of optimization weighted least of squares Wirtinger (WLSW) proposed by the authors. The WLSW its objective function is quadratic and the constraints are linear, for that, the propose model is convex optimization. Finally these methods are compared use several metric error.

articleTitle: Voltage Detection Algorithm for Characteristics of Grid-Forming Converters Under Voltage Drop Events
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: Clarifying the impact and output voltage of the grid- forming converter under grid voltage drop events is a key step in voltage drop management. Focusing on the grid-forming converter with a control structure based on virtual synchronous generator technology and the current limiting section, this paper explores the operating mechanism of the grid-forming converter during voltage drops and the characteristic waveforms and variations of the output voltage under grid voltage drop events are obtained. Aiming at the waveform characteristics of the output voltage, a voltage detection algorithm based on the coordinate-free transform method and morphological filters is proposed, which eliminates the intermediate section of constructing the virtual three-item voltage, and can directly separate the direct flow of the voltage signals. The morphological filters can better extract the cosine periodic fluctuation and change components in the characteristic waveforms of the voltage. Finally, a detection model is built using Simulink, the model verifies the feasibility and effectiveness of the new detection algorithm combined coordinate- free transform method with the morphological filter, as well as its high adaptability to the characteristic waveforms of the grid- forming converter.

articleTitle: An Overview of Fault Current Limiter and Power System Overvoltage Problem:Towards the Application of Better Operational Stability
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: After the fault current limiter(FCL) is connected to the power grid, it can effectively solve the problem of excessive short-circuit current in the power system. However, its dynamic characteristics, stray capacitance and other parameters are coupled with the power grid parameters, which may have an impact on the overvoltage of the system to some extent. This article first introduces the classification and causes of system overvoltage, as well as its harm to different power equipment, clarifying the harmfulness of overvoltage. Secondly, the effects of current limiters on operating overvoltage, power frequency overvoltage, and their own overvoltage were elaborated. Research has shown that current limiters have both positive and negative effects on various overvoltages. Finally, preliminary suppression measures were discussed for the overvoltage caused by the current limiter, such as parallel capacitors at both ends of the current limiter and optimizing its parameters.

articleTitle: Gearbox Oil Temperature Prediction for 1.5 MW Wind Turbine Based on Stacking Model
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: Wind turbines are complex systems integrating machinery, electrical, and control, and they often operate in places with harsh environments. This can easily cause the wind turbine to malfunction or even shut down, resulting in significant economic losses and safety accidents. In recent years, big data technology and machine learning algorithms have been constantly tried to be applied to fault diagnosis and prognosis of wind turbines, especially gearbox. In this paper, the oil temperature predicted model of the gearbox is constructed to detect anomalies. First, the wind speed and power in the supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) system are used to remove anomaly data points using the density-based spatial clustering of applications with noise (DBSCAN) algorithm, and the grid search method is used to optimize the two input parameters of the DBSCAN algorithm, and then the quartile method is used for further data preprocessing. Second, filter algorithm is conducted to determine the significant features, and these selected features are used to build the predicted model. Third, a fusion model based on the stacking strategy in ensemble learning is established to characterize the normal working status of the gearbox in wind turbines. The application of the presented method to gearbox oil temperature prediction is evaluated by a real-world gearbox normal process. The experimental results show that the proposed method embraces a good ability to predict.

articleTitle: Simulation Study on Thermal Runaway Propagation of Lithium-Ion Battery Pack for Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: This Thermal runaway is a key safety problem for lithium batteries, and the catastrophic effects can be effectively avoided by suppressing further propagation in the face of the single battery cell sudden thermal runaway. In this study, we have developed a thermal runaway propagation model tailored for a 94kWh lithium battery pack, accounting for intricate physical processes such as self-generated heat, water cooling, heat transfer, and erupting gas flow. To enhance model accuracy, a dual-battery thermal propagation model was constructed to calibrate cell parameters, achieving an average test error of less than 10%. Subsequently, a battery pack model was formulated using the calibrated cell parameters to assess various strategies for mitigating thermal runaway propagation. Our findings reveal that optimizing the structure of the thermal resistant layer by reducing its thermal conductivity can effectively suppress thermal runaway propagation.

articleTitle: Static and Dynamic Load Altering Attack Detection Based on Tractable Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Power Energy Systems and Applications (ICoPESA)
abstract: Internet of Things (IoT)-enabled loads are gradually penetrating into the power grids. However, the vulnerabilities of IoT can be leveraged maliciously to compromise high-wattage appliances. This gives the adversaries a chance to launch load altering attacks(LAAs), which may result in system instability or even large-scale blackouts. Thus, detecting the LAAs in real time is a crucial task for grid operators. In this paper, we propose a novel detection method that can detect both static LAAs (SLAAs) and dynamic LAAs (DLAAs). In the end, we provide a tractable optimization-based reformulation that improves the scalability, and as such practicality, of the proposed method. This method can detect both static and dynamic LAAs in a unified frame. The experiments at last demonstrate the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed detection method.
